title: Hybrid inference supplier resilience playbook for procurement and go/no-go decisioning
creator: Maya Chen
description: Synthesize competitive and supplier-resilience signals into a concise playbook teams can use when choosing between hosted, dedicated, and private deployment options. Focus on failure modes that impact enterprise procurement (model outages, regional capacity loss, quantization regressions, supplier price shocks) and produce concrete decision thresholds, contract guardrails, and a lightweight runbook teams can operationalize during onboarding and renewal discussions.
goals: Create a repeatable scoring rubric for supplier resilience across latency, availability, quantization compatibility, and contractual remedies
Deliver a procurement-focused playbook with must-have contract clauses and fallback runbooks for high-risk enterprise verticals (finserv, healthcare)
Produce a short checklist for solutions and sales to use during vendor selection and renewal conversations
acceptance_criteria: Rubric spreadsheet covering 10 supplier signals (regional capacity, SLO history, quant fallback availability, export controls, support SLAs) reviewed by Legal and Sales
Playbook one-pager and 6-step runbook created and published to Confluence
Two pilot procurement reviews run with Sales on live deals to validate the rubric (feedback captured)
Draft contract clause language for fallback capacity and model-substitution remedies reviewed by Legal
deliverables: Playbook doc: Confluence page + printable one-pager
Short internal training slide deck (10 slides)
Post-pilot retrospective notes and recommended changes
comments: 2026-03-01 Maya Chen: Ticket created after cross-functional intake with Sales and Legal. Problem statement: enterprise buyers repeatedly ask for concrete remedies and costed fallback plans when open-model hosting changes. Initial ask: create a procurement-friendly playbook.

2026-03-03 Liam O'Connor: Scoping session notes: focus on five failure scenarios (regional outage, model regression after quantization, model provider license change, sudden price increase, and export-control restriction). Proposed signals list attached to Sheet draft.

2026-03-05 Ravi Singh (Sales Eng): Shared two anonymized RFPs where customers required explicit fallback SLAs — will arrange for redacted copies. Action: Sales will introduce us to two active deals for pilot run-throughs.

2026-03-07 Sofia Patel (Legal): Legal provided template fallback clause language and highlighted that minimum remedies vary by region (EU vs US) — flagged need for Legal sign-off on every template iteration.

2026-03-08 Engineering (Runtime Reliability): Supplied telemetry snapshot (last 12 months) for three regions; flagged recurring short-duration capacity spikes in APAC for dedicated pools. Link to dashboard included.
2026-03-10 Maya Chen: Draft rubric v0.2 uploaded to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ResiliencePlaybook (internal). Please review and comment by 2026-03-13.

2026-03-11 Liam O'Connor: Pilot deal #1 scheduled for 2026-03-16 with Solutions and Sales; objectives: validate rubric weighting and verify Sales checklist language is usable in pre-RFP conversations.
2026-03-12 Diane Park: Customer Success volunteered to run the checklist against three existing enterprise customers to validate perceived risk thresholds. Added as a stakeholder.

2026-03-12 Maya Chen: Note — schedule constrained by Legal availability for contract language review. Proposed mitigation: create two tiers of clause language (recommended vs expedited) to keep pilots moving.
decision_log: 2026-03-04: Decided to prioritize enterprise verticals with regulatory constraints (finserv, healthcare) for playbook coverage (vote: Legal + Sales + PM)
2026-03-06: Chose a hybrid scoring approach (quantitative score + qualitative notes) vs purely numeric to account for supplier-provided metrics opacity
2026-03-09: Agreed to require a model-substitution guarantee or pre-approved fallback inventory for P0 contracts — Legal to draft language
2026-03-11: Agreed to limit initial pilot to two deals to get rapid feedback; expand after iteration
